summary: This note is an encyclopedia-style overview of Winchester, the county town of Hampshire, England, located at the western end of the South Downs National Park along the River Itchen. It gives the city's location relative to London and Southampton, its population at the 2011 Census, and the population of the wider City of Winchester district. It also covers the city's Roman and Iron Age origins and its major landmarks and institutions, including Winchester Cathedral and Winchester College.
one_line: Winchester is the historic county town of Hampshire, England, with Roman origins, a famous cathedral and Winchester College.
key_facts: Winchester is a city and the county town of Hampshire, England.
Winchester lies at the western end of the South Downs National Park, along the course of the River Itchen.
Winchester is situated 60 miles (97 km) south-west of London.
Winchester is 13.6 miles (21.9 km) from Southampton, its closest city.
At the time of the 2011 Census, Winchester had a population of 45,184.
The wider City of Winchester district, which includes towns such as Alresford and Bishop's Waltham, has a population of 116,800.
Winchester developed from the Roman town of Venta Belgarum.
Venta Belgarum developed from an Iron Age oppidum.
Winchester Cathedral is the city's major landmark.
Winchester Cathedral is one of the largest cathedrals in Europe.
Winchester Cathedral has the longest nave and overall length of all Gothic cathedrals in Europe.
The City of Winchester is a local government district.
The University of Winchester is located in the city.
Winchester College is the oldest public school in the United Kingdom still using its original buildings.
